format:

<!--
Build cost page for the VIBE results website.

Everything here is computed from columns export_results.py already writes:
build_time, index_size, qps, recall — plus n from results/data-info.parquet.

Grouping note: `params` is "<algorithm name>|<query parameters>", and for several
algorithms the name itself contains query parameters (e.g. FaissIVFSQ(..., n_probe=1)),
so it is not an index-configuration key. build_time is: every run that shares an
index build shares its build_time. All queries below group by (algorithm, build_time),
which recovers the true number of builds (hnswlib: 9 builds behind 144 param strings
on landmark-nomic).
-->

## Column {width=20%}

:::{.card .flow}
Build time and query time are both wall-clock seconds on a single core, so they add
up. Pick a dataset and the recall you need, then use the legend to highlight
algorithms.
:::

```{ojs}
//| output: false
db = DuckDBClient.of({
  summary: FileAttachment("results/summary.parquet"),
  algorithm_basics: {file: FileAttachment("algorithms_basics.csv"), header: true},
  data_info: FileAttachment("results/data-info.parquet")
});

datasets = db.sql`
  select distinct dataset from summary
  where dataset not like '%-id-%' order by dataset;
`
// LEFT JOIN + coalesce: five algorithms in the published results are missing from
// algorithms_basics.csv (hnswq(faiss), nsgq(faiss), pag, pdx, symqg). A NATURAL JOIN
// drops them silently; treating an unknown algorithm as CPU keeps them visible.
algorithms = db.sql`
  select distinct algorithm from summary natural left join algorithm_basics
  where coalesce(is_gpu, false) = ${gpu_algorithms} order by all;
`
palette = Array.from(d3["schemeTableau10"]);
ncolors = palette.length;
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
mutable_non_gpu_color_map = new Mutable(new Map([
  ["hnswlib", palette[0]],
  ["ivf(faiss)", palette[1]],
  ["glass", palette[2]],
]));
non_gpu_color_map = mutable_non_gpu_color_map.generator

mutable_gpu_color_map = new Mutable(new Map([
  ["cuvs-cagra", palette[0]],
  ["faiss-gpu-ivf", palette[1]],
  ["ggnn", palette[2]],
]));
gpu_color_map = mutable_gpu_color_map.generator

color_map = gpu_algorithms ? gpu_color_map : non_gpu_color_map
colorOf = (a) => color_map.has(a) ? color_map.get(a) : "#cccccc"
```

```{ojs}
//| fill: false
//| width: 20%
viewof selected_dataset = Inputs.select(
  datasets.map(d => d.dataset),
  {value: "landmark-nomic-768-normalized", label: "select dataset"}
);
k_values = db.sql`select distinct k from summary;`
viewof k_value = Inputs.select(k_values.map(d => d.k), {value: 100, label: "value of k"});
viewof recall_target = Inputs.range([0.8, 1], {step: 0.01, value: 0.9, label: "recall target"});
viewof ternary_pick = Inputs.select(
  new Map([["fastest at the target", "qps"], ["cheapest to build", "build"],
           ["smallest index", "size"]]),
  {value: "qps", label: "triangle config"}
);
viewof ternary_scale = Inputs.select(
  new Map([["doublings worse (log₂)", "log"], ["times worse", "ratio"]]),
  {value: "log", label: "triangle scale"}
);
viewof overview_metric = Inputs.select(
  new Map([["× the cheapest build there", "ratio"], ["absolute seconds", "abs"]]),
  {value: "ratio", label: "overview cells"}
);
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Algorithm type
//| fill: false
viewof gpu_algorithms = {
  const control = html`
    <div class="form-check form-switch d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
      <input class="form-check-input mt-0" type="checkbox" role="switch" id="gpu-toggle-build">
      <label class="form-check-label" for="gpu-toggle-build">GPU algorithms</label>
    </div>
  `;
  const toggle = control.querySelector("input");
  Object.defineProperty(control, "value", {get: () => toggle.checked});
  return control;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
d3.select("#legend-build")
  .selectAll("div")
  .data(algorithms)
  .join("div")
  .style("border-bottom", d => `solid 6px ${(color_map.has(d.algorithm)) ? color_map.get(d.algorithm) : "lightgray"}`)
  .style("border-top", "solid 1px lightgray")
  .style("border-left", "solid 1px lightgray")
  .style("border-right", "solid 1px lightgray")
  .style("border-radius", "4px")
  .style("padding-right", "5pt")
  .style("padding-left", "5pt")
  .on("click", (event, d) => {
    const key = d.algorithm;
    let cm = new Map(color_map);
    if (cm.has(key)) {
      cm.delete(key);
    } else {
      const usedColors = new Set(cm.values());
      const color = palette.find(color => !usedColors.has(color));
      if (color !== undefined) cm.set(key, color);
    }
    if (gpu_algorithms) mutable_gpu_color_map.value = cm;
    else mutable_non_gpu_color_map.value = cm;
  })
  .text(d => d.algorithm);
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Algorithms
html`
<div class="algorithm-list-content">
  <p>Select up to ${ncolors} algorithms to highlight them in the plots.</p>
  <div id="legend-build" style="display: flex; flex-direction: row; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4pt;">
  </div>
</div>
`
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the data
// One row per index build: what it cost, how large it is, and the best
// throughput it can deliver at the selected recall (null if it never gets there).
builds_arrow = db.sql`
  SELECT algorithm,
         build_time,
         any_value(index_size) AS index_size,
         max(recall) AS best_recall,
         max(CASE WHEN recall >= ${recall_target} THEN qps END) AS qps_at_target,
         -- arg_max ignores rows whose ordering value is NULL, so these describe the
         -- fastest configuration of this build that actually reaches the target
         arg_max(params, CASE WHEN recall >= ${recall_target} THEN qps END) AS best_params,
         arg_max(recall, CASE WHEN recall >= ${recall_target} THEN qps END) AS recall_at_best
  FROM summary NATURAL LEFT JOIN algorithm_basics
  WHERE dataset = ${selected_dataset}
    AND k = ${k_value}
    AND coalesce(is_gpu, false) = ${gpu_algorithms}
  GROUP BY algorithm, build_time
  ORDER BY algorithm, build_time;
`
builds = Array.from(builds_arrow)          // Arrow tables are not plain arrays
usable = builds.filter(d => d.qps_at_target !== null && d.qps_at_target > 0)

dataset_size_arrow = db.sql`
  SELECT n FROM data_info WHERE dataset = ${selected_dataset};
`
dataset_size = Array.from(dataset_size_arrow).map(d => Number(d.n))[0] ?? null

// per algorithm: the sweep, and the single build a paper would report
sweep = Array.from(d3.rollup(builds, v => ({
    n_builds: v.length,
    n_usable: v.filter(d => d.qps_at_target !== null).length,
    sweep_seconds: d3.sum(v, d => d.build_time),
    cheapest_usable: d3.min(v.filter(d => d.qps_at_target !== null), d => d.build_time),
    reported: v.filter(d => d.qps_at_target !== null)
                .reduce((m, d) => (m === null || d.qps_at_target > m.qps_at_target) ? d : m, null)
  }), d => d.algorithm))
  .map(([algorithm, o]) => ({algorithm, ...o}))
  .filter(d => d.n_usable > 0)

reported = sweep.map(d => ({algorithm: d.algorithm, ...d.reported,
                            queries_equiv: d.reported.build_time * d.reported.qps_at_target}))
alg_by_build = sweep.slice().sort((a, b) => a.cheapest_usable - b.cheapest_usable).map(d => d.algorithm)
// the build the reader last clicked in the sweep panel
mutable_selected_build = new Mutable(null)
selected_build = mutable_selected_build.generator

fmtN = d3.format(".3s")
// SI on seconds reads badly ("3.49ks"), so durations get human units
secs = (v) => v < 90 ? (v < 10 ? v.toFixed(1) : d3.format(".3r")(v)) + " s"
            : v < 5400 ? (v / 60).toFixed(0) + " min"
            : (v / 3600).toFixed(1) + " h"
// label only decade ticks: a log axis with .3s on every minor tick is unreadable
fmtDecade = (v) => Math.abs(Math.log10(v) - Math.round(Math.log10(v))) < 1e-6 ? fmtN(v) : ""
```

## Column

### Row

::: {.card title="Every build in the sweep, not just the one that gets reported" width=72%}
```{ojs}
// Clicking a dot reports the fastest configuration that build reaches at the
// current recall target. Plot renders one <circle> per datum in data order, so the
// circles inside each dot mark line up with the array that produced them.
{
  mutable_selected_build.value = null;   // a new dataset/recall invalidates the old pick

  const missed = builds.filter(d => d.qps_at_target === null);
  const reaches = builds.filter(d => d.qps_at_target !== null);

  const chart = Plot.plot({
    style: {fontSize: "10pt"},
    marginLeft: 150,
    marginRight: 20,
    height: 26 * alg_by_build.length + 46,
    x: {type: "log", grid: true, label: "build time (seconds) →", tickFormat: fmtDecade},
    y: {domain: alg_by_build, label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY(alg_by_build, {y: d => d, stroke: "#eee"}),
      Plot.dot(missed, {
        x: "build_time", y: "algorithm", r: 3.5, stroke: "lightgray", fill: "none",
        title: d => `${d.algorithm}\n${secs(d.build_time)}\nnever reaches recall ` +
                    `${recall_target} (best ${d.best_recall.toFixed(3)})`
      }),
      Plot.dot(reaches, {
        x: "build_time", y: "algorithm", r: 3.5, fill: d => colorOf(d.algorithm), fillOpacity: 0.75,
        title: d => `${d.algorithm}\n${secs(d.build_time)}\n${fmtN(d.qps_at_target)} qps — click for details`
      }),
      Plot.tickX(reported, {
        x: "build_time", y: "algorithm", stroke: "black", strokeWidth: 2, strokeOpacity: 0.75
      })
    ]
  });

  const markData = [missed, reaches];
  chart.querySelectorAll("g[aria-label='dot']").forEach((g, gi) => {
    const rows = markData[gi];
    if (!rows) return;
    Array.from(g.querySelectorAll("circle")).forEach((circle, i) => {
      const d = rows[i];
      if (!d) return;
      circle.style.cursor = "pointer";
      circle.addEventListener("click", () => {
        chart.querySelectorAll("circle").forEach(c => {
          c.removeAttribute("stroke-width");
          if (c.getAttribute("stroke") === "black") c.setAttribute("stroke", "none");
        });
        circle.setAttribute("stroke", "black");
        circle.setAttribute("stroke-width", 2);
        mutable_selected_build.value = d;
      });
    });
  });
  return chart;
}
```
Each dot is one index build; **click one** to inspect it. Hollow dots never reach the
recall target with any search parameters. The black tick marks the build a paper would
quote — the one whose configuration gives the highest throughput at this recall.
:::

```{ojs}
//| title: Selected build
//| width: 28%
{
  const muted = "color: #5a6570;";
  if (!selected_build) {
    return html`<div style="${muted} font-size: 0.9rem;">
      Click a dot in the sweep to see what that build costs and which configuration
      gets the most out of it at the current recall target.</div>`;
  }
  const d = selected_build;
  const row = (k, v) => html`<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem;">
      <span style="${muted}">${k}</span><span style="font-weight: 500; text-align: right;">${v}</span>
    </div>`;
  const params = (d.best_params ?? "").split("|");

  if (d.qps_at_target === null) {
    return html`<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; font-size: 0.85rem;">
      <div style="font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 600;">${d.algorithm}</div>
      ${row("build time", secs(d.build_time))}
      ${row("index size", `${fmtN(d.index_size * 1024)}B`)}
      ${row("best recall reached", d.best_recall.toFixed(4))}
      <div style="${muted} margin-top: 0.3rem;">
        No search parameters take this build to recall ${recall_target}.</div>
    </div>`;
  }
  return html`<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; font-size: 0.85rem;">
    <div style="font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 600;">${d.algorithm}</div>
    ${row("build time", secs(d.build_time))}
    ${row("index size", `${fmtN(d.index_size * 1024)}B`)}
    ${row("fastest at the target", `${fmtN(d.qps_at_target)} qps`)}
    ${row("recall there", d.recall_at_best.toFixed(4))}
    ${row("best recall this build reaches", d.best_recall.toFixed(4))}
    <div style="${muted} margin-top: 0.4rem;">index</div>
    <div style="font-family: var(--bs-font-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere;">${params[0]}</div>
    <div style="${muted}">query</div>
    <div style="font-family: var(--bs-font-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere;">${params[1] ?? "—"}</div>
  </div>`;
}
```

### Row

```{ojs}
//| title: "Build cost in queries you could have answered instead"
Plot.plot({
  style: {fontSize: "10pt"},
  marginLeft: 150,
  marginRight: 70,
  height: 22 * reported.length + 46,
  x: {type: "log", grid: true, label: "build cost in query-equivalents →", tickFormat: fmtDecade},
  y: {domain: reported.slice().sort((a, b) => a.queries_equiv - b.queries_equiv).map(d => d.algorithm), label: null},
  marks: [
    dataset_size ? Plot.ruleX([dataset_size], {stroke: "gray", strokeDasharray: "3 3"}) : null,
    Plot.ruleY(reported, {
      y: "algorithm", x1: d => d3.min(reported, x => x.queries_equiv) / 2, x2: "queries_equiv",
      stroke: d => colorOf(d.algorithm), strokeWidth: 5, strokeOpacity: 0.6
    }),
    Plot.dot(reported, {x: "queries_equiv", y: "algorithm", r: 3.5, fill: d => colorOf(d.algorithm)}),
    Plot.text(reported, {
      x: "queries_equiv", y: "algorithm", text: d => fmtN(d.queries_equiv),
      textAnchor: "start", dx: 8, fill: "currentColor", fontSize: 10
    }),
    Plot.tip(reported, Plot.pointer({
      x: "queries_equiv", y: "algorithm",
      title: d => `${d.algorithm}\nbuild ${secs(d.build_time)} × ${fmtN(d.qps_at_target)} qps\n` +
                  `= ${fmtN(d.queries_equiv)} queries' worth of work`
    }))
  ].filter(d => d)
})
```

::: {.card title="Why query-equivalents"}
Build time in seconds is only meaningful on the machine that produced it. Multiplying
it by the throughput that same machine achieves — `build_time × QPS` — cancels the
machine speed to first order and states the build cost in the only currency the index
earns back: queries answered. The dashed line is one pass over the dataset.
A build costing far more query-equivalents than the dataset has points is one that
only a long-lived, heavily queried index repays. A true hardware-independent measure
would count distance computations during construction, which VIBE does not record
today; this is the closest thing available from stored results.
:::

### Row

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// ------------------------------------------------- the ternary design space
// RUM (Athanassoulis et al., EDBT 2016) places access methods in a read/update/
// memory triangle by argument. The ANN analogue — query speed / build cost /
// memory — can be placed by measurement instead: for each algorithm take the
// build that gives the best throughput at the recall target, express each of its
// three costs as excess over the best value any algorithm achieves here, and use
// the three excesses as barycentric coordinates. An algorithm that is best on an
// axis has zero excess there and lands on the opposite edge; position says where
// an algorithm's disadvantage sits, marker size says how much of it there is.
// which of an algorithm's builds represents it in the triangle. The default —
// its fastest at the recall target — is the configuration every other panel
// reports, and it systematically minimises the query excess, so the other two
// options are offered: they move the whole picture, which is the point.
ternary_base = Array.from(d3.group(usable, d => d.algorithm), ([algorithm, v]) => ({
  algorithm,
  ...(ternary_pick === "qps" ? v.reduce((m, d) => d.qps_at_target > m.qps_at_target ? d : m)
    : ternary_pick === "build" ? v.reduce((m, d) => d.build_time < m.build_time ? d : m)
    : v.reduce((m, d) => d.index_size < m.index_size ? d : m))
}))

best_qps = d3.max(ternary_base, d => d.qps_at_target)
best_build = d3.min(ternary_base, d => d.build_time)
best_size = d3.min(ternary_base, d => d.index_size)

ROOT3_2 = Math.sqrt(3) / 2

// "log": how many doublings worse than the best on that axis — treats the three
// axes symmetrically, so the one with the widest spread does not own the geometry.
// "ratio": how many times worse, which is easier to read but lets the widest axis
// dominate.
excess = ternary_scale === "log" ? (x) => Math.log2(x) : (x) => x - 1

ternary = ternary_base.map(d => {
  const e_query = excess(best_qps / d.qps_at_target);   // slower than the fastest
  const e_build = excess(d.build_time / best_build);    // more expensive to build
  const e_mem = excess(d.index_size / best_size);       // larger than the smallest
  const total = e_query + e_build + e_mem;
  const s = total > 0 ? [e_query / total, e_build / total, e_mem / total] : [1/3, 1/3, 1/3];
  return {
    ...d, e_query, e_build, e_mem, total,
    s_query: s[0], s_build: s[1], s_mem: s[2],
    x: 0.5 * s[0] + s[2],
    y: ROOT3_2 * s[0]
  };
})

// triangle outline and the 25 / 50 / 75 % grid inside it
corners = [{x: 0.5, y: ROOT3_2}, {x: 0, y: 0}, {x: 1, y: 0}, {x: 0.5, y: ROOT3_2}]
ternary_grid = [0.25, 0.5, 0.75].flatMap(v => [
  // constant query share
  {x1: 0.5 * v, y1: ROOT3_2 * v, x2: 0.5 * v + (1 - v), y2: ROOT3_2 * v},
  // constant build share
  {x1: 1 - v, y1: 0, x2: 0.5 * (1 - v), y2: ROOT3_2 * (1 - v)},
  // constant memory share
  {x1: v, y1: 0, x2: v + 0.5 * (1 - v), y2: ROOT3_2 * (1 - v)}
])
// textAnchor and dy are constants in Plot, not channels, so each corner label is
// its own mark
corner_query = [{x: 0.5, y: ROOT3_2, t: "slower to query"}]
corner_build = [{x: 0, y: 0, t: "expensive to build"}]
corner_mem = [{x: 1, y: 0, t: "large index"}]
// 22 points crowd the bottom edge, so label only what the reader chose plus the
// single most balanced index; everything else is in the tooltip
best_overall = ternary.reduce((m, d) => d.total < m.total ? d : m)
ternary_labelled = ternary.filter(d => color_map.has(d.algorithm) || d === best_overall)
```

```{ojs}
//| title: "Where each algorithm's disadvantage sits"
Plot.plot({
  style: {fontSize: "10pt"},
  aspectRatio: 1,
  marginTop: 30,
  marginBottom: 34,
  marginLeft: 30,
  marginRight: 30,
  x: {axis: null, domain: [-0.04, 1.04]},
  y: {axis: null, domain: [-0.03, ROOT3_2 + 0.03]},
  r: {type: "sqrt", range: [3, 16]},
  marks: [
    Plot.link(ternary_grid, {x1: "x1", y1: "y1", x2: "x2", y2: "y2", stroke: "#e8e8e8"}),
    Plot.line(corners, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#999"}),
    Plot.text(corner_query, {x: "x", y: "y", text: "t", textAnchor: "middle", dy: -14, fill: "currentColor"}),
    Plot.text(corner_build, {x: "x", y: "y", text: "t", textAnchor: "start", dy: 18, fill: "currentColor"}),
    Plot.text(corner_mem, {x: "x", y: "y", text: "t", textAnchor: "end", dy: 18, fill: "currentColor"}),
    Plot.dot(ternary, {
      x: "x", y: "y", r: "total",
      fill: d => colorOf(d.algorithm),
      fillOpacity: d => color_map.has(d.algorithm) ? 0.85 : 0.5,
      stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.75,
      title: d => `${d.algorithm}\n` +
        `${fmtN(d.qps_at_target)} qps — ${(best_qps / d.qps_at_target).toFixed(1)}× off the fastest\n` +
        `${secs(d.build_time)} build — ${(d.build_time / best_build).toFixed(1)}× the cheapest\n` +
        `${fmtN(d.index_size * 1024)}B index — ${(d.index_size / best_size).toFixed(1)}× the smallest\n` +
        `share: query ${(100 * d.s_query).toFixed(0)}% · build ${(100 * d.s_build).toFixed(0)}%` +
        ` · memory ${(100 * d.s_mem).toFixed(0)}%`
    }),
    Plot.text(ternary_labelled, {
      x: "x", y: "y", text: "algorithm", dy: -12, fontSize: 9, fill: "currentColor"
    })
  ]
})
```

::: {.card title="Reading the triangle"}
Each algorithm is placed by its **excess over the best value on this dataset**: how far
it is from the fastest index in throughput, from the cheapest in build time, and from the
smallest in index size. Those three excesses, normalized to sum to one, are the
coordinates. The scale control decides how "far" is counted — *doublings worse*, which
weighs the three axes symmetrically, or *times worse*, which is easier to read but lets
whichever axis happens to have the widest spread pull every point toward its corner.

An algorithm that is best on one axis has no excess there and lands on the **opposite
edge** — `lorann` on the build corner's far edge because it holds the smallest index,
`rabitq-ivf` on the edge away from build because nothing builds faster. **Position is
balance, marker size is magnitude**: a small dot near a corner is a good index with one
mild weakness; a large dot in the same place is a bad trade. The top half of the triangle
stays empty on most datasets, and that is itself a result — at a fixed recall the spread
in throughput is far narrower than the spread in what the indexes cost to build and to
store.

Each algorithm is represented by one of its builds, and which one matters: the default —
its fastest configuration at the recall target — is the one every other panel reports,
and it is also the one that minimises the algorithm's distance from the query corner.
Switching the config control to *cheapest to build* or *smallest index* re-places every
point, and the movement is the trade being made.

The reference values are set by whichever algorithm is best on each axis, so a single
unusually small or fast index moves everyone else's coordinates — that is a property of
normalizing to the best, and the same caveat applies to the relative build-time column in
the VIBE paper. Raw values are in the tooltip.
:::

### Row

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// ------------------------------------------- build cost and size across datasets
// Ignores the dataset selector on purpose: these are the overviews.
overview_arrow = db.sql`
  SELECT dataset, algorithm,
         min(build_time) AS cheapest_build,
         min(index_size) AS smallest_index
  FROM summary NATURAL LEFT JOIN algorithm_basics
  WHERE k = ${k_value}
    AND recall >= ${recall_target}
    AND coalesce(is_gpu, false) = ${gpu_algorithms}
    AND dataset NOT LIKE '%-id-%'
  GROUP BY dataset, algorithm;
`
sizes_arrow = db.sql`SELECT dataset, n FROM data_info;`
dataset_n = new Map(Array.from(sizes_arrow).map(d => [d.dataset, Number(d.n)]))

overview_rows = Array.from(overview_arrow)
overview_datasets = Array.from(new Set(overview_rows.map(d => d.dataset)))
  .sort((a, b) => (dataset_n.get(a) ?? 0) - (dataset_n.get(b) ?? 0))
shortDataset = (d) => d.replace(/-\d+-/, "-")

// One matrix builder, used for both resources: cell value is the best this
// algorithm can do on that axis while still clearing the recall target, and the
// ratio is to whichever algorithm does best on that dataset.
overviewFor = (metric) => {
  const value = (d) => metric === "build" ? d.cheapest_build : d.smallest_index * 1024;
  const floor = d3.rollup(overview_rows, v => d3.min(v, value), d => d.dataset);
  const cells = overview_rows.map(d => ({...d, v: value(d), ratio: value(d) / floor.get(d.dataset)}));
  const algorithms = Array.from(d3.rollup(cells, v => d3.median(v, d => d.ratio), d => d.algorithm))
    .sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]).map(d => d[0]);
  // midpoint of the (log) colour ramp, for deciding label contrast
  const mid = overview_metric === "ratio"
    ? Math.sqrt(d3.max(cells, d => d.ratio))
    : Math.sqrt(d3.min(cells, d => d.v) * d3.max(cells, d => d.v));
  return {cells, algorithms, mid};
}

overviewPlot = (metric) => {
  const {cells, algorithms, mid} = overviewFor(metric);
  if (cells.length === 0) {
    return html`<div style="color: #5a6570;">Nothing reaches recall ${recall_target} on any dataset.</div>`;
  }
  const label = (d) => metric === "build" ? secs(d.v) : fmtN(d.v) + "B";
  return Plot.plot({
    style: {fontSize: "9pt"},
    width: Math.max(780, 34 * overview_datasets.length + 170),
    marginLeft: 150,
    marginBottom: 190,
    marginTop: 8,
    height: 21 * algorithms.length + 200,
    x: {domain: overview_datasets, tickRotate: -45, label: null, tickFormat: shortDataset},
    y: {domain: algorithms, label: null},
    color: {
      type: "log",
      scheme: metric === "build" ? "blues" : "purples",
      label: overview_metric === "ratio"
        ? (metric === "build" ? "build time ÷ cheapest build there" : "index size ÷ smallest index there")
        : (metric === "build" ? "build time (seconds)" : "index size (bytes)")
    },
    marks: [
      Plot.cell(
        d3.cross(overview_datasets, algorithms).map(([dataset, algorithm]) => ({dataset, algorithm})),
        {x: "dataset", y: "algorithm", fill: "#f2f2f2", inset: 0.5}
      ),
      Plot.cell(cells, {x: "dataset", y: "algorithm", inset: 0.5,
        fill: d => overview_metric === "ratio" ? d.ratio : d.v}),
      Plot.text(cells, {
        x: "dataset", y: "algorithm", fontSize: 8,
        text: d => overview_metric === "ratio"
          ? (d.ratio < 10 ? d.ratio.toFixed(1) : d3.format(".0f")(d.ratio))
          : label(d),
        fill: d => (overview_metric === "ratio" ? d.ratio : d.v) > mid ? "white" : "black",
        title: d => `${d.algorithm}\n${shortDataset(d.dataset)}\n` +
          (metric === "build"
            ? `cheapest build reaching recall ${recall_target}: ${secs(d.v)}`
            : `smallest index reaching recall ${recall_target}: ${fmtN(d.v)}B`) +
          `\n${d.ratio.toFixed(1)}× the best on this dataset`
      })
    ]
  });
}
```

::: {.card title="Across datasets: the cheapest build that reaches this recall"}
```{ojs}
overviewPlot("build")
```
Rows are ordered by median relative cost, columns by dataset size, so a row that darkens
to the right scales worse than its neighbours. A grey cell means that algorithm never
reaches recall ${recall_target} on that dataset with any configuration. Drag the recall
slider to watch cells drop out.
:::

### Row

::: {.card title="Across datasets: the smallest index that reaches this recall"}
```{ojs}
overviewPlot("size")
```
The same matrix for memory: the smallest index each algorithm can get away with while
still clearing the recall target, against the smallest any algorithm manages on that
dataset. Rows are ordered independently of the build-time matrix — an algorithm can be
cheap on one axis and expensive on the other, and the two orderings differing is the
finding.
:::
